keep_playing_why: B had a visible score system (best score, 3 stars, orders, combos, call-wave-early bonus) and each new enemy type changed how I built, so I kept finding better lines and wanted to re-run levels for stars. A gave me a good drift and smash multiplier once I found it, but 2 minutes passed before I understood the goal and crashes cost 5 to 8 seconds of dead waiting under a magnet. I never felt pulled to restart A, while I wanted to three-star the Stovetop in B.
better_made_why: B has a complete shell: tutorial hints, hub with six levels and a star count, orders, result screens with best score, readable HUD, consistent art, and no stuck states in 9 minutes. A has the better 3D look, sound and juice (rain, smoke, vibration, ambience), but I got wedged on trees repeatedly, the goal was hidden for two minutes, and the respawn drops you at zero speed into the same bend. B's weaker point is almost no music.
furthest_A: Score 10,988 at 541 s, 41 mi, in-game clock past 01:36 (night into rain), best drift payout +822 at x2.0, one 1,472-point crash loss.
furthest_B: Cleared The Cutting Board (3 stars, 14,180), The Stovetop (2 stars, 36,010, beat the Jar boss) and The Sink (3 stars, 25,210) on the second try after losing once; was in Sunday Lunch (level 4) at wave 9 of 12 with 15 of 20 bites left and score 11,700 at 542 s; hub showed 8 of 15 stars.
